tables.name: Inn: what stands out
tables.description: One thing guests remember about the place.
rows: A huge hearth takes up the whole back wall and the innkeeper is proud of it.
Every table wobbles. The regulars put folded notes under the legs and never agree who should fix it.
The ceiling is hung with hundreds of old boots, one for every guest who ever left without paying.
The soup is the same every day, and it is so good that nobody asks what is in it.
A caged raven watches the room and calls out the name of whoever walks in, usually wrong.
The cellar door is locked with three padlocks and the innkeeper changes the subject when asked.
A long table is always kept free in the corner. Nobody will say for whom.
The walls are covered with chalk drawings by travelers, some of them very old maps.
The beer comes from a brewery two valleys away and costs double, but it is worth it.
A retired sergeant runs the door. Fights are over before they begin.
There is a well in the middle of the common room, covered with a heavy wooden lid.
The upstairs rooms are rented by the hour and the owner insists it is for sleeping.

tables.name: Tavern guest
rows: A merchant counting coins twice and still not happy with the sum.
Two farmhands arguing about whose turn it is to buy the next round.
A bard tuning a lute with one string missing.
A tired courier with mud up to the knees who eats without looking up.
An old woman knitting in the corner who hears everything.
A young noble in plain clothes who is not very good at being plain.
A dwarf telling the same story about a bridge for the third time tonight.
A pair of guards off duty, pretending not to watch the door.
A pilgrim sharing bread with a stray dog.
A card player who is winning too much to be lucky.
A traveling healer selling cures to anyone who coughs.
A shy student surrounded by books, a candle and a cold supper.
A scarred mercenary asking quietly who is hiring.
A drunk sailor swearing the sea is following him inland.
A tinker with a cart full of pots, hinges and one surprising sword.
A hooded stranger who paid for a room and has not touched the drink.
A cheerful cook from the next village who came to steal the soup recipe.
A child sweeping the floor for a bowl of stew.
A poacher trying to sell a very large hare to the very tired innkeeper.
A town clerk with a bundle of notices he cannot find a nail for.

tables.name: Tavern: who is here tonight
tables.description: A table inside a table: how busy the room is decides how many guests are drawn.

tables.name: Shop
tables.description: A kind of shop and who runs it. The owner is drawn from the names of any people.
rows: Chandler: candles, lamp oil and tinder, run by {{name-any}}.
Herbalist: dried bundles, tinctures and honest advice, run by {{name-any}}.
Cobbler: boots, buckles and a bench full of unfinished repairs, run by {{name-any}}.
Bookbinder: ledgers, journals and a few books nobody has asked about, run by {{name-any}}.
Baker: bread before dawn and gossip after, run by {{name-any}}.
Fletcher: arrows by the dozen and bows by appointment, run by {{name-any}}.
Rope maker: cord, nets and knots for every occasion, run by {{name-any}}.
Pawnbroker: a little of everything and no questions, run by {{name-any}}.
Tailor: cloth, thread and an eye for who can pay, run by {{name-any}}.
Smith: tools, nails and horseshoes, run by {{name-any}}.
Apothecary: powders, salves and a locked cabinet, run by {{name-any}}.
Curio shop: shelves of strange things with handwritten labels, run by {{name-any}}.

tables.name: Shop: an odd thing for sale
tables.description: One unusual item in the window. Prices roll themselves.
rows: A lantern that burns without oil. It gives off a little less light every night. [[2d6+5]] gp.
A walking stick that always points slightly to the left. [[1d6]] gp.
A jar of honey from bees that only feed on night flowers. [[1d4]] gp.
A mirror that shows the room as it was an hour ago. [[3d6]] gp.
A pair of boots that are always dry. [[2d6]] gp.
A bell that rings once whenever a lie is told near it. [[4d6]] gp.
A cloak with a hood that is always a little too big. [[1d6+1]] gp.
A small box that cannot be opened but sounds like it contains coins. [[2d4]] gp.
A candle that smells of the owner's grandmother's kitchen. [[1d8]] sp.
A map of a town that no one has ever heard of. [[2d6+3]] gp.
A flute that only plays one tune, but plays it perfectly. [[1d10]] gp.
A sack of seeds that sprout in a single night, then wilt by morning. [[1d4+2]] gp.
